title: Platform privacy controls can exist while practical data control remains uncertain
source_unit: FTC Section 6(b) staff report based on responses from nine large social-media and video-streaming companies
geography: United States platform market and companies reviewed by the FTC

observations.period: FTC report published September 2024; company practices reviewed through the 6(b) inquiry period

denominator.unit: large social-media and video-streaming companies responding to FTC 6(b) orders

retention.value: companies could indefinitely retain large amounts of data

sharing.value: broad data sharing with third parties and affiliates was reported

deletion.value: some companies did not delete all user data after deletion requests

control_quality.value: privacy, data minimization, and retention practices were described as inadequate

observations.method: FTC Section 6(b) review of company responses concerning data collection, retention, sharing, privacy controls, and user and non-user information.
observations.uncertainty: The inquiry is a company-practice review, not a census of platforms or users and not an independent audit of every data store, deletion request, affiliate, inference, or downstream recipient.
observations.subgroup: Nine large social-media and video-streaming companies; users, non-users, children, and other data subjects appear within the reviewed practices but are not a single prevalence denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: Legal, security, and trust-and-safety retention exceptions can be legitimate; a reported practice gap does not prove that every request failed or that every person experienced harm.

related_sources.claim: FTC summarizes the findings of its 6(b) review of nine companies and their data practices.
FTC describes its privacy and security enforcement authority and current case context.

boundary: This record measures reported platform practices and FTC staff assessment for nine companies. It does not establish a user-level deletion failure rate, individual harm, downstream data use, actual reappearance, safety, trust, or durable exit.
